text: {"distance_m": 12, "reasoning_short": "This is a rough estimate from typical threshold data. A spot 4 mm wide with 30% contrast is a small, moderately low-contrast target. For tiny spots, detection depends on contrast times area (Ricco's law). At normal indoor light, published thresholds suggest a 30% spot needs to span about 1 to 1.2 arcmin, slightly more than a fully black dot would. 4 mm divided by about 1.15 arcmin (0.00033 rad) gives roughly 12 m. At the pure 1 arcmin acuity limit it would be about 13.7 m."}
